Full record: docs/production-hardening-plan.md section 9.

items.title: Kafka prepared-transaction resume: wire-level FindCoordinator + EndTxn(commit) in-doubt resolution at HA restore-point selection, using pid/epoch captured from librdkafka's stats callback and staged in the checkpoint; CONFIRMED advances only on the broker's explicit acknowledgement
items.risk: A checkpoint completing whose broker commit had not executed when the worker died was the one window neither the sink nor the client could close; resolution commits the genuine orphan and advances the restore point past the interval, with the commit-confirmed bounded contract as the floor on every failure.
tests: TxnResumeWire/TxnResume (10, hermetic: byte-for-byte golden frame, parsers vs truncation/foreign correlation, fake broker: happy/fenced/unsupported/no-identity/unreachable, resolver through the registry)
ResolutionFixture (9: walk order, all-handles-must-commit, every conservative stop)
TxnResumeLive (3, real Redpanda: fork-crashed orphan committed exactly-once end to end, fenced identity refused, wrapper stages resolvable handle and erases on commit)

KafkaExactlyOnceTest.AnOrphanedBrokerTransactionIsCommittedAcrossACoordinatorFailover (whole-chain HA e2e, real processes + real broker: held commit loads the orphan by construction, worker dies pre-commit, leader dies, standby's recovery resolves the orphan on the broker, CONFIRMED advances, output totally clean; mutation-checked with a false-confirm resolver linked into the job plugin - caught as 3 MISSING records)
items.limitations: in-incarnation restarts now resolve too (PR-14); non-flexible protocol versions only (FindCoordinator v1/v2, EndTxn v1) and no SASL - both fall back, never guess. Revisit against librdkafka KIP-939 support when it ships. e2e round findings: producer identity is now captured with a bounded wait in KafkaSink::open() (stats tick at 100ms), closing the pre-first-tick window where staged handles were unresumable; the HA-recovery-drops-job-on-no-capacity finding is closed by PR-13.

items.title: HA recovery parks a capacity-refused job and retries from the manifest when a worker registers, instead of dropping it
items.risk: A takeover that outpaced the worker supervisor logged 'recovery failed: insufficient free slots' and a RUNNING job silently ceased to exist until the next failover, its checkpoints intact on disk. Parking + manifest-replay makes recovery converge whenever capacity returns; the already-running guard makes the retry idempotent, and every non-capacity failure still drops loudly.
tests: HaFailoverTest.ARecoveredJobParkedForCapacityRunsWhenAWorkerReturns (integration: worker killed BEFORE the leader, submit slot-wait shrunk to 1.5s via the new --submit-wait-for-slots-ms flag so the park is reached, park pinned from the coordinator log, worker restarted only AFTER the park, output exactly-once; mutation-checked by disabling the park - caught as 38 MISSING records after 96s)
items.limitations: the retry keeps trying for as long as the coordinator leads (no give-up bound - a parked job with no workers is the operator's capacity problem, surfaced by the park warning); typed InsufficientSlotsError distinguishes capacity from every other submit rejection.

items.title: In-incarnation restarts hold the redeploy behind in-doubt resolution, so the prepared-transaction resume covers ordinary worker loss, not just HA takeover
items.risk: The common failure (worker dies pre-commit, coordinator survives) fell back to the bounded replay contract. The restart is now staged behind an off-thread resolution when a tracked job's drain completes with a completed-but-unconfirmed gap: nothing deploys while the broker is being asked, so nothing can fence the orphan - resolution and restore-point selection stay one decision. A refused/failed resolution releases the restart unchanged; a wedged resolver hits a 90s watchdog backstop that fails the job loudly naming the resolution.
tests: KafkaExactlyOnceTest.AnOrphanedBrokerTransactionIsCommittedOnAnInIncarnationRestart (real coordinator survives, loaded orphan, restart held, resolver commits on the broker, restore advances, submitter exits 0, output totally clean; mutation-checked by never holding the restart - caught on the held-restart vacuity line with clink_node rebuild verified by mtime)
items.limitations: all four restart_job_locked_ trigger sites are gated; the resolution thread mirrors the drain-complete readiness check (drained covers expected). Non-tracked jobs and jobs with no confirmed<completed gap stage nothing and restart exactly as before.

items.title: Restart-drain readiness is coverage, not emptiness: the watchdog kick fires a restart whose expected set a fold shrank to already-drained keys
items.risk: The soak's three-CI-sighting wedge (watch item 63). Draining credits restart_drained_keys and COVERS restart_drain_expected; a second-worker fold erases the dead worker's keys from both sets. When the survivor's drain ack lands before the fold, the expected set becomes covered-but-nonempty and readiness - re-evaluated only on a new SubtaskFinished - is never observed again: the ready restart sits until the 30s drain deadline fails the job with a phantom 'survivors did not drain'. restart_drain_covered_() is now THE readiness predicate at every restart trigger site.
tests: RestartDrainReadiness.AFoldAfterTheLastDrainAckStillFiresTheRestart (deterministic: DrainFakeWorker pair scripts the exact frame order - victim dies silently, survivor errors, survivor's other subtask drains, replacement registers - against a real coordinator over real sockets; asserts the redeploy arrives well inside the drain deadline. Pre-fix mutant (emptiness kicks) wedges 16s and fails; fix passes in 0.5s.)
items.limitations: diagnosed entirely from the serial soak run's dumped logs (the d8faf3c instrumentation); the soak itself remains the probabilistic end-to-end witness and stays serial - its 30s deadline is a correctness bound and is unchanged.

items.title: SASL (and wired TLS) for the prepared-transaction resume, so the resolver reaches brokers the sink can already talk to
items.risk: The sink declares sasl_plaintext/sasl_ssl/ssl (librdkafka passthrough) but the resume wire path speaks plaintext-no-auth only, so on an authenticated cluster every in-doubt resolution refuses and the bounded contract carries it. DELIVERED: SASL/PLAIN on both resume connections with env-sourced credentials (CLINK_KAFKA_RESUME_SASL_*), local refusal of unspoken mechanisms, honest fallback shapes. REMAINING scope: (1) SaslHandshake v1 + SaslAuthenticate v1 (PLAIN) on both resume connections, golden-frame UTs + FakeBroker refusal arms; (2) credentials read from the coordinator's environment at RESOLVE time - never staged in the checkpoint handle; (3) TLS via the existing ConnectFn seam (impls/tls), with the doc stating PLAIN-over-plaintext leaks credentials and recommending sasl_ssl; (4) DockerKafka gains a SASL mode (Redpanda enable_sasl + superuser) and a live arm proving resolve-with-creds commits and resolve-without refuses loudly.
tests: TxnResume SASL arms vs the fake broker: authenticated resume commits and presents the RFC 4616 payload on BOTH connections; unknown mechanism refused locally before any dial; handshake refusal surfaces the broker's enabled mechanisms; bad credentials refused with the broker's message and no EndTxn attempted; no-credentials against a SASL-only listener falls back as TransportError. Mutation-checked twice: auth-failure-treated-as-success caught by the bad-credentials arm; mechanism-gate-removed caught by the unknown-mechanism arm.

TxnResumeSaslLive (live, real SASL-required Redpanda via DockerKafkaOptions{sasl}): a PLAIN handshake is refused by the SCRAM-only broker naming SCRAM; no credentials falls back as TransportError on the connection drop. The pinned Redpanda v24.2.7 rejects PLAIN in sasl_mechanisms validation (verified empirically), so the PLAIN happy path stays hermetic by necessity.

TxnResumeTls (hermetic, real TLS sessions via a self-signed cert and accept_tls_connection): the resume commits over a verified TLS session; the resolver dials TLS end to end when CLINK_KAFKA_RESUME_TLS_CA is set; an unusable CA refuses loudly with a plaintext broker standing ready to catch a downgrade. Mutation-checked: the resolver ignoring the CA env was caught by BOTH the dial-through assertion and the no-downgrade arm.
items.limitations: complete: SASL/PLAIN wire half, live refusal arms against a real SASL broker, and the env-gated TLS dialer (wired at the TOP-LEVEL CMakeLists - impls/tls is processed after impls/kafka, so an if(TARGET) inside the kafka lists is false forever; export-safe since clink_tls shares the export set and libclink already links it). SCRAM deferred (crypto surface); the PLAIN happy path live requires a broker pin with PLAIN support; KIP-939 revisit unchanged.

items.title: SCRAM-SHA-256 for the prepared-transaction resume, closing the authenticated-broker happy path live
items.risk: SCRAM is what Kafka clusters (and the pinned Redpanda, which rejects PLAIN outright) actually enable, so the resume's SASL support was refusal-only in practice. A from-scratch RFC 5802/7677 client (clink/kafka/scram.hpp, OpenSSL HMAC/PBKDF2/SHA-256 via the clink::tls gate) now runs the two-round exchange on both resume connections and VERIFIES THE SERVER: signature mismatch, non-extending nonce, and sub-4096 iteration counts are refused - a broker that cannot prove knowledge of the credentials never receives EndTxn.
tests: TxnResumeScram.TheRfc7677VectorIsReproducedExactly (the whole exchange against the RFC's published user/pencil vector - the only non-circular gate a from-scratch SCRAM client can have)

TxnResumeScram attack arms: reflected/foreign nonce, KDF-downgrade iteration count, e= error replies, and a forged server signature scripted by a crypto-free fake broker (mutation-checked: skipping the signature verification is caught)

TxnResumeSaslLive.AScramAuthenticatedResumeCommitsAGenuineOrphan (the crown arm: an orphan produced with librdkafka's own SCRAM - an independent implementation - resumed by this client against real Redpanda, server signature verified, records committed exactly; wrong credentials refused by the real broker)
items.limitations: SHA-256 only (what brokers enable); no channel binding (matching every Kafka client - transport pairing is the TLS dialer); RFC 5802 username escaping but no full SASLprep (non-ASCII usernames are the broker's refusal, not a silent mis-encode). consume_all gained an extra_conf param for authenticated drains. KIP-939 revisit unchanged.
